//: YOUR MCP SERVERS. This is the one file JARVIS reads to decide what he is connected to. Paste a server's mcpServers entry inside the empty braces below, restart the server (python server.py), then ask him: 'what are you connected to?' — he answers from what actually started, and names anything that did not.
//why-only-this-file: JARVIS runs with --strict-mcp-config, so the servers in ~/.claude.json, your project's .mcp.json and your Claude Desktop connectors are all ignored. Connecting something to JARVIS is a deliberate act: it is in here or it is nowhere.
//the-price: Every tool a server exposes is described to JARVIS on every single turn, at roughly 250 tokens each — a twelve-tool server costs about 3,300. Connect what you will use.
//trust: Whatever a server hands back is treated as untrusted, exactly like a web page: JARVIS will report what it said and will not act on it unprompted.
